 Oral Judgment

(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE R.NATARAJ) M.F.A.No.200251/2025 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Court of the III Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Raichur (henceforth referred to as 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.563/2022 vide judgment and award dated 20.02.2024.
M.F.A.No.202305/2024 is filed by the insurer challenging its liability to pay the compensation awarded by the Tribunal in the aforesaid case.

2. The claimant filed M.V.C.No.563/2022 under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (henceforth referred to as 'M.V.Act, 1988') claiming compensation Rs.41,00,000/- for the injuries suffered in a road accident on 01.10.2022, when he was riding pillion on a motorcycle bearing Reg.KA-36/Y-5437 which was tail ended by a lorry bearing Reg.NL-01/AE-6256.
As a result of the accident, the claimant suffered his right hand was crushed and later was amputated above the elbow.
The claimant claimed he NC: 2026:KHC-K:1043-DB HC-KAR was aged 56 years and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month as a mason.
He therefore claimed compensation from the owner and insurer of the lorry.
3. The insurer on the other hand contested the claim petition on the ground that the rider of the motorcycle was negligent and he was responsible for the accident.
The insurer also challenged the quantum of compensation on the ground that the same was excessive.
4. The Tribunal after considering the oral and documentary evidence, held that the claimant had suffered an amputation of the right hand above the elbow.

It considered the age of the claimant at 56 years and treated his income at a sum of Rs.14,750/- and determined the following compensation :
1. Loss of income and future prospects Rs.14,01,840/-
2. Towards medical expenses Rs.1,78,087/-
3. Towards pain, suffering and loss of Rs.25,000/- amenities 4.

Towards special diet, transportation Rs.22,000/-
attendance charges Total Rs.16,26,927/-
NC: 2026:KHC-K:1043-DB HC-KAR 5.
It directed the insurer to pay the compensation along with interest at 6% per annum.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation and the liability, both the claimant as well as the insurer are in appeal.

sentences.text:
The learned counsel for the claimant contended the tribunal had considered the disability suffered by the claimant at 80% without assessing the functional disability suffered by the claimant,
who was a mason.

She contended that the Tribunal failed to award adequate compensation towards loss of income during the course of treatment, and adequate compensation towards pain and suffering, loss of amenities and also an artificial limb.
She therefore prays that the impugned judgment and award passed be modified and the compensation be enhanced.
7. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurer however contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is excessive.
She also contends that the claimant is not entitled for an artificial limb as there is no evidence to suggest that an artificial limb could be fixed.

She also NC:
2026:KHC-K:1043-DB HC-KAR contends that the driver of the motorcycle was negligent and he was responsible and therefore the owner and insurer of the motorcycle ought to have been arrayed as a party before the Tribunal.
8. We have considered the submissions made by learned counsel for the claimant as well as the learned counsel for the insurer.
9. A perusal of the records shows that the claimant had suffered amputation above the elbow.
The claimant appears to be an able bodied man and the contention of the claimant that he was working as a mason cannot be disbelieved.

10. Having regard to the fact that the Tribunal has considered his notional income at a sum of Rs.14,750/-, along with 10% loss of future prospects in view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co.Ltd., v. Pranay Sethi and others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, we consider the said NC: 2026:KHC-K:1043-DB HC-KAR income assessed by the Tribunal is just and proper.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd., v. Pranay Sethi and others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has assessed the disability suffered by the claimant at 80% which we consider it to be appropriate as the same is in line with the disability assessed under the provisions of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923.
However, the Tribunal ought to have granted compensation towards loss of income during treatment, pain and suffering, loss of amenities, cost of an artificial limb etc.

Consequently, we consider it appropriate to enhance the compensation as follows:
1. Pain and suffering Rs.1,00,000/-
2. Loss of income due to injuries Rs.14,01,840/- suffered 3. Loss of income during the period of 44,250/- treatment of 3 months 4. Loss of amenities Rs.1,00,000/-
5.

Medical expenses Rs.1,78,087/-
6. Transportation, special diet and Rs.40,000/- attendant charges 7.
Towards artificial limb Rs.50,000/-

sentences.text: As regards the liability of the insurer, though it is alleged that the rider of the motorcycle was negligent, it NC: 2026:KHC-K:1043-DB HC-KAR is in the evidence that the motorcycle was tail ended by the lorry and therefore no negligence could be attributed to the rider of the motorcycle.
Consequently, the insurer is liable to pay the compensation.
12. In that view of the matter, MFA No.200251/2025 filed by the claimant is allowed in part.

Compensation of Rs.16,26,927/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to sum of Rs.19,14,177/-,
which is payable by the insurer along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the date of claim petition till the date of realisation.

The insurer shall deposit the enhanced compensation within a period of 30 days from the date of receipt of a copy of this order along with accrued interest, failing which interest shall be paid at 9% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realisation and the excess interest paid shall be recovered from the person responsible for the delay in depositing the compensation.
13. It is needless to mention that the claimant shall not be entitled to interest for a period of 254 days.
MFA No.202305/2024 filed by the insurer
is dismissed.
15. Any amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal for necessary orders.
